profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded semiconductor and computing company, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, trading on the NASDAQ under the ticker NVDA. The company reported revenue of $215,938,000,000 for the fiscal year ending January 25, 2026, according to its most recent 10-K filing. The page captured here focuses on NVIDIA's AI model and inference infrastructure offerings rather than its broader hardware business.

NVIDIA's Nemotron is described by the company as a family of multimodal, open AI models built for agentic AI applications, covering reasoning, multimodal vision, retrieval-augmented generation, speech, and safety tasks. The site describes Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as a variant aimed at helping agents complete specialized tasks faster, and mentions NeMo Switchyard as a routing tool that directs each step to an appropriate model. NVIDIA publishes model weights, training datasets, and training techniques under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which the company describes as permissive and allowing commercial deployment without requiring attribution to NVIDIA. Nemotron models are also available as NVIDIA NIM microservices, which the company describes as inference microservices for secure and scalable enterprise deployment, with that option requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license. Supporting tools referenced on the site include NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, NeMo, and compatibility with open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM. Bryan Catanzaro, identified as VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is cited on the site in connection with the vision behind Nemotron.

The held facts note 174 legal exposure entries associated with California, though no specific cases are recorded in the data. NVIDIA holds a page in the registry with CIK 0001045810 and has two tracked products, Nemotron and NIM, consistent with the focus of the harvested site content.
